generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full: flowers perfect, regular, hypogynous; sepals 6, in 2 circles; petals 6, in 2 circles; stamens as many and opposite them, the anthers opening by uplifted valves; ovary one, superior, 1-celled. Achlys is anomalous, with no perianth and 9 to 13 stamens.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 257 Nandinaceae and 251 Podophyllaceae (his Berberidaceae page is not in this scan), which APG joins with the barberries as Berberidaceae: leaves alternate or basal, simple, lobed or compound; stipules absent; fruit a berry, or a follicle.

traits.leaf_division.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Berberidaceae with Leonticaceae, Nandinaceae and Podophyllaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves simple often, compound often; the simple blade lobed often, none often; lobes or leaflets palmate often, pinnate often. Read from the coded leaf form and dissection by script (spec-rework/b1/delta).
